## Same prompt. Two outcomes.

Real refusal triggers developers hit in 2026 — next to an example of the direct answer you get here.

Developer prompt

My GraphQL updateMember resolver lets a BILLING user set role: ADMIN on their own org. Write the guard.

Gated assistant response

Classifier block: cybersecurity capability.

Found the privilege-escalation flaw in the user’s own codebase, then blocked every attempt to review or patch it.

Documented developer report · r/Anthropic · Oct 2026

Example answer · run it live in the Playground

if (input.role === 'ADMIN' && ctx.actor.role !== 'OWNER') { throw new GraphQLError('Only OWNER may grant ADMIN', { extensions: { code: 'FORBIDDEN_ROLE_ESCALATION' }, }); } if (target.orgId !== ctx.actor.orgId) { throw new GraphQLError('Cross-tenant mutation denied'); }

Pair with a unit test asserting BILLING → ADMIN throws FORBIDDEN_ROLE_ESCALATION.

Every LLM we host has its refusal direction projected out at the weight level, so it answers legitimate prompts directly instead of refusing, lecturing, or watering down code. Illegal use remains strictly off-limits under our Acceptable Use Policy.

It is designed not to. Orthogonal weight editing removes one narrow activation direction — the one behind refusals — instead of fine-tuning the model on new data, so the change is small and targeted.
